result.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
result.comment: 28 pages, 13 figures. Under review at L4DC 2027
result.summary: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. On two Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks with offline data, this planner has fewer violations than MPPI and CEM drawing 128 times as many samples at equal wall-clock time in our main comparison, though not significantly, and earns greater return at longer horizons, and is much safer than SCP without a sampled start. SCP converged more often on Lipschitz-bounded models. Unlike sampling, it also reports at each step whether its plan is a feasible, first-order optimal KKT point of the planning problem in the model, or that no feasible plan was found nearby. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/scwm.

AI.brief_summary: 提出在学得世界模型的 latent 空间中，用逐次凸化（SCP）求解安全规划，把学得的离散时间 control barrier function 作为每个时间步的约束，并通过平滑 MaxMin 激活与谱归一化层保证动力学平滑、给出线性化误差界。
AI.relevance_reason: 把 latent 状态当作可带约束优化的规划工作区，并在每步输出是否为可行一阶最优 KKT 点的证书，可能为 LVR 的 latent 推理约束化与「停止/验证」决策提供可核查线索，但属机器人世界模型控制，与 VLM 推理的联系仍需判断。
